newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel limits CRP acres to 14 million.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel limits CRP acres to 14 million.

text.p: The House Appropriations Committee Thursday passed a bill that would cap enrollment in the Conservation Reserve Program at 14 million acres during fiscal 1997 (Oct-Sept).

The action came during committee debate on an emergency spending bill to aid victims of floods and other natural disasters. As drafted by subcommittee, the legislation included a 14 million-acre cap on the CRP.
By a 22-26 vote the full committee rejected an amendment by Washington Republican Rep. George Nethercutt to eliminate the cap.
The Agriculture Department had planned to sign up 19 million acres. The spending bill may be debated by the full House as early as next week.
"Anyone who cares about environmental protection ought to be concerned," Nethercutt said.
Supporters of the cap, led by New York Rep. James Walsh, argued that most of the benefits of the CRP program had gone to Midwest farmers and it was time to provide some geographic equity.
He said the committee was committed to the full 36 million acres allowed under the five-year farm law, but wanted to give farmers in other areas a chance to participate.
"The problem is the Midwest, God love them, gets 90 percent of the acreage," he said.

The emergency spending bill also cuts the amount allocated for USDA's export credit program to $3.5 billion from $5.5 billion for fiscal 1997 (Oct-Sept). It also reduces the appropriation for the Export Enhancement Program to $10 million from $100 million.
